paper_metadata.title: Python-Integrated Quantum–Classical Computing Framework for Intelligent Time-Series Prediction

experiments.description: Python-integrated hybrid quantum-classical variational circuit for time-series prediction on real financial and synthetic nonlinear datasets, evaluated against classical baselines and with scalability tests over varying circuit depths and qubit counts.

algorithm.variant: Python-integrated hybrid quantum-classical variational quantum circuit for time-series forecasting
algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized rotation gates with entanglement layers
algorithm.optimizer: Adam or SGD; also described as a naive optimizer in the workflow
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Early stopping; training loss curves generally converged after about 35 iterations; loop ends when convergence conditions are met or after all encoded instances have been processed

hyperparameters.alpha: weighting factor in L_total = alpha * L_quantum + (1 - alpha) * L_classical
hyperparameters.learning_rate: reported as tuned; learning rate decay used
hyperparameters.batch_size: reported as managed through configuration files; mini-batch strategies used for massive datasets

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not specified; constant seeds used for repeated runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Raw time-series windows are normalized and mapped to quantum states using rotation parameter gates; expectation values from the circuit are used as classical feature vectors
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize combined loss L_total = alpha * L_quantum + (1 - alpha) * L_classical

problem_instance.description: Time-series forecasting on synthetic nonlinear data and real financial series

classical_postprocessing: assemble expectation values into Python dict
